packs.title: Desert and Discovery
packs.promise: Explore Phoenix through desert forms, museum discoveries and wide views.

q.s: Connect a visible detail with information supplied by its maker or museum.
st: Choose an object or artwork in an open gallery.
Read its label and note the credited maker or community exactly as presented, plus one material or visual detail.
Write a question prompted by those details; avoid guessing cultural meaning from appearance.

q.s: Discover how distance changes what an artwork shows you.
st: Choose a work in an open gallery that has room for observation.
Compare its overall arrangement with a detail seen from a closer permitted position.
Draw two small abstract studies of those views without copying the whole artwork.

q.s: Look at desert plants as a collection of different lines.
st: Choose a short open garden path after admission.
Find three different plant outlines without touching plants or leaving the path.
Draw the outlines and record a plant name only when a label identifies it.

packs.title: Roosevelt Row to Hance Park
packs.promise: Move from street art to garden paths and the cultural spaces beside Hance Park.

q.s: Create a new arrangement of those colors using different shapes from the mural.
st: Choose a visible public mural from a sidewalk without entering a lot or alley.
Identify three colors that organize the composition and note any visible artist credit.
Create a new arrangement of those colors using different shapes from the mural.

q.s: Write one observation that comes from looking, keeping it separate from label information.
st: Check the gallery’s current entrance and public hours on its site.
Choose an openly displayed artwork or exhibition notice and record its credited artist, title and material when listed.
Write one observation that comes from looking, keeping it separate from label information.

q.s: Mark the point where a visitor would decide which way to go.
st: From the public sidewalk or an open visitor area, find three different uses shown by the venue’s signs or directory.
Draw a small map of how those uses relate to the central gathering space.
Mark the point where a visitor would decide which way to go.
